reasons.specificity: The concept matrix accurately distinguishes technique as social creation from capitalism’s quantitative rationality and identifies their different argumentative roles.
reasons.anchoring: The substantive quotations occur in the named works and generally support the stated meanings, qualifications, methods, and aligned labor claim.
reasons.non_obviousness: The analysis usefully distinguishes local efficiency from social-historical neutrality, the real-rational from rational mastery, and chronological order from demonstrated uptake.
reasons.coherence: The core comparison is consistent, but the enormous appended scope apparatus repeatedly labels confirmed findings “inconclusive” and introduces unexplained review codes and statuses.
reasons.usefulness: The opening matrix and paired-change table are strong, but the requested one-page artifact is overwhelmed by repetitive inventories, ledgers, and unsupported review-process metadata.
reasons.hallucination_risk: Most textual claims are well supported, but the invented-looking D-number provenance, reported inspections, evidence-record failures, and review statuses have no basis in the supplied sources.

decisive_errors.claim: The conclusion characterizes “Technique” as offering “a general ontology and politics of technique.”
decisive_errors.counter_passage: “those who perceive that ‘the essence of technique is absolutely not to do with technique’, reimmerse at once this essence in an ontology which removes it from the decisive moment of the human world — from making/doing.”
decisive_errors.why: Calling the essay’s method a general ontology obscures its explicit resistance to removing technique from social-historical making/doing.

score.one_line: An excellent, well-anchored comparative reading and matrix is substantially damaged by severe failure of the one-page brief and by extraneous, unsupported scope-review machinery.
